clue.text: Love to roam at Manx resort with zest

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, shown as the letter O
to roam is to range over the land
Peel is a seaside town on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A romantic urges a partner to wander a seaside town on the Isle of Man with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zest' looks like enthusiasm, but here it is the citrus skin used in cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is the grated outer skin of a citrus fruit used for flavouring.

clue.text: A pitcher with a double reed in it?

definitions.text: A pitcher with a double reed in it?

parts.words: A pitcher with a double reed in it?
parts.note: a 'pitcher' is not a jug but something that produces musical pitch, a woodwind instrument sounded through a double reed

explanation.surface: A jug with a pair of rushes standing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: This woodwind instrument produces its notes through a double reed mouthpiece.

clue.text: Back Lincoln Square

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of President Abraham Lincoln
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T can stand for square

explanation.surface: A reference to Abraham Lincoln and a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a person is to support or assist them, often in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Sock, for example, knitted for thick-skinned types?

indicators.note: knitted suggests strands worked together into a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sock is offered as an example of something knitted for tough customers.
explanation.definitionFit: These lizards have tough, scaly skin, so they are jokingly called hardy creatures.

clue.text: Plain sherry-glass found in emigrants' wagon

parts.note: a prairie is a broad grassy plain
a schooner is a tall glass for sherry

explanation.surface: A grassy plain and a glass of sherry turn up in a settler's covered wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: This covered wagon carried settlers westward across North America in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Bind book

explanation.surface: An instruction to tie up a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage is to commit someone by promise, and also to reserve or hire in advance.

clue.text: Assemble class

explanation.surface: A teacher tells a group of pupils to gather.
explanation.definitionFit: To form is to put together, and a form is a school year group.

clue.text: Regular job, calling with post?

parts.note: a trade or profession, and also the military holding of a post or territory, read through 'regular' soldiers taking a post

explanation.surface: A postman's daily round of house calls.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's job or vocation is their line of work, and soldiers seizing a position also carry out one.

clue.text: A single? Mid-off is tricky!

indicators.note: off means out of order or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator notes that taking one run to the fielder at mid-off is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-off is a cricket fielding position, but here 'off' rearranges A SINGLE MID.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deceptive or likely to give a false impression is tricky.

clue.text: Rook settled before storm

parts.note: a matter settled is over, finished
to storm a position is to charge at it

explanation.surface: A chess rook stays put before an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' looks like the chess piece or the bird, but is the verb meaning to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to swindle them, taking far too much money.

clue.text: Book of achievements?

parts.note: a book of the New Testament whose title also means deeds or things done

explanation.surface: A record of someone's accomplishments.
explanation.definitionFit: Deeds are things done, and the Acts of the Apostles is a book of the Bible.

clue.text: The case for the prosecution

parts.note: a grammatical case, here the one sounding like that used by someone who charges a defendant

explanation.surface: The argument set out by the barrister bringing charges.
explanation.definitionFit: This grammatical case marks a verb's direct object, and its name echoes the word for charging someone.

clue.text: Diversions of men, set a sum to throw about…

indicators.note: throwing about suggests scattering, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Men amuse themselves by tossing a sum of money around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to throw about' rearranges MEN SET A SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainments and pastimes are things that divert attention pleasantly.

clue.text: Bottle about as old as we are

parts.note: c (circa) is the abbreviation for about
something as old as we are is of our age

explanation.surface: A bottle of wine is roughly the same vintage as the drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for nerve or courage, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, bottle means nerve or bravery.

clue.text: … larks to include a thousand holidaymakers

indicators.note: one word taking in another signals a container

parts.note: larks and capers are both pranks or escapades
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers get up to pranks, a thousand of them.
explanation.definitionFit: People staying in tents or caravans on vacation are holidaymakers.

clue.text: Constituent of select origins

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is a part taken from the following words

explanation.surface: A voter comes from a choice background.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter in a district is one of its constituents.

clue.text: Stops butterflies

explanation.surface: Something halts a swarm of flying insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Punctuation marks are called stops, and the comma is also a kind of butterfly with a comma-shaped mark.

clue.text: The Spanish variety of peas roll by

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: a variety is a different arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A type of Spanish pea rolls past.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that rolls by passes or slips away.

clue.text: Green pistachio nuts chopped by editor

indicators.note: chopped means cut up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A green salad of pistachio nuts is chopped by a magazine editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' rearranges PISTACHIO NUTS; 'Green' means naive, not the colour of pistachios.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or naive, lacking worldly refinement.

clue.text: Delight in Madeira, endlessly, when travelling

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving around, so the letters are rearranged
endlessly means the word Madeira loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A tourist enjoys Madeira while journeying around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last A of MADEIRA to give MADEIR, and 'when travelling' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight in something is to regard it with pleasure and approval.

clue.text: Young bird found in golf hole, timid to begin with

parts.note: an eagle is a hole played two under par in golf

indicators.note: to begin with means take the first letter of the word timid

explanation.surface: A shy fledgling is spotted on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A chick of the large bird of prey is called this.

clue.text: To be remembered as an Eastern warehouse

explanation.surface: A storehouse in Asia deserves to go down in history.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'go down' in history is to be remembered; a godown is a warehouse in India and East Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: To be recorded in history is an idiom with this phrase, and in Asia a godown is a storehouse.

clue.text: Evangelist Elmer's platform?

explanation.surface: A preacher named Elmer stands on a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Elmer Gantry is the hypocritical preacher in Sinclair Lewis's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional preacher's surname is also a frame bearing a crane or railway signals.

clue.text: Red-hot water boiler, say?

parts.note: 'Red' is Russian, so a Russian urn for heating water for tea

explanation.surface: A glowing kettle for heating water.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian urn for boiling water to make tea, with 'Red' meaning Soviet.

clue.text: Area of devotional island

indicators.note: an area of a word is a stretch of its letters taken from inside it

explanation.surface: A region known for its religious island.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'devotional'; Iona is a Scottish island famed for its abbey.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, a centre of early Christianity.

clue.text: Ambassador has no love for covetousness

indicators.note: has no means a letter is removed from the word for ambassador

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomat sent as an ambassador
love is nil in tennis, shown as the letter O

explanation.surface: A loveless diplomat who covets others' possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealous longing for what others have is a synonym for covetousness.

clue.text: A body of detectives should be sharp

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A police detective unit ought to be quick-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart or biting taste is sharp, as is a cutting remark.

clue.text: Formulate potassium pick-me-up from sea-food organisms…

parts.note: to formulate a scheme is to plan it
K is the chemical symbol for potassium
a tonic is a restorative drink

explanation.surface: A chemist mixes a potassium tonic out of sea creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea-food' means the tiny drifting organisms fish feed on, not seafood for people.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes drifting microscopic marine life eaten by many sea animals.

clue.text: … how could it be otherwise in Winchelsea?

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is lodged inside the place name that follows

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about how things could be different in an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Winchelsea is a small town in East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in another way or instead, a synonym for otherwise.

clue.text: Sweetheart begins to dally having looked radiantly happy

indicators.note: begins means take the first letter of the word Sweetheart

parts.note: to dally is to linger or tarry
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: A lover starts to linger after gazing with joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamily idealistic and glowing with happiness.
